newsitem.title: USA: BankAmerica said eyeing Robertson Stephens.
newsitem.headline: BankAmerica said eyeing Robertson Stephens.

text.p: BankAmerica Corp., which has expressed its desire to get into the securities underwriting business, is reportedly interested in acquiring investment banking firm Robertson Stephens & Co.
The San Francisco Chronicle reported Friday the San Francisco-based banking giant is said to be in talks with Robertson Stephens about a possible merger.

Neither Robertson Stephens or BankAmerica would comment on speculation, but employees within Robertson Stephens said a rumour that the two firms were holding discussions was circulating within the company.
Thomas Theurkauf, analyst with Keefe Bruyette Woods, also said he heard the rumour from several members of the investment community while in San Francisco earlier this week.

While declining to comment, a spokesman for BankAmerica reiterated that the banking company plans to get into the underwriting business by growing from within, acquiring an underwriter or forming an alliance.
Analysts said Robertson Stephens and BankAmerica would make a good fit.
"Robertson Stephens has a big presence in the equity underwriting business, which is what BankAmerica is looking for," said Raphael Soifer at PaineWebber.
Some analysts estimated BankAmerica may pay upwards of $500 million for Robertson Stephens.

Robertson Stephens has $4.2 billion under management. It completed 125 stock offerings, raising $8.6 billion, and advised on 50 deals totalling $9 billion in 1996. The firm, which has swelled from 30 employees in 1981 to 800 currently, has total capital of $75 million, a spokeswoman said.
Speculation about banks buying brokers has grown since government restrictions were eased on securities underwriting by banks.
